Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

rule verb

to govern

also govern, reign, rule over, command (an army), govern the country, govern (a province)

classical

Cic. Rosc. Am. 131: cum sōlus rem pūblicam regeret (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Sen. 37: tantam domum … Appius regēbat
Traupman 180, 373

regō, regere, rēxī, rēctum

verb, third conjugation

rule, govern, direct

Of a state, a household, and oneself (animum rege, Hor. Ep. 1.2.62).

Other words

  • imperō, imperāre, imperāvī, imperātum — command, rule over

    verb, first conjugation, with the dative · also used · classical · Hor. Ep. 1.2.62–63: quī nisi pāret, imperat; Traupman 178

    To give orders and have them obeyed; the opposite is pārēre, obey.

  • rēgnō, rēgnāre, rēgnāvī, rēgnātum — reign, be king

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Rep. 2.17: Rōmulus cum septem et trīgintā rēgnāvisset annōs (Lewis & Short); Publil. Sent. R 19

    Of a king’s rule, and of anyone who has his own way.

  • gubernō, gubernāre, gubernāvī, gubernātum — steer; govern a state

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Rosc. Am. 131: orbemque terrārum gubernāret (Lewis & Short); Traupman 179, 323: rem pūblicam gubernāre; Traupman 323

    Properly to steer a ship (Greek κυβερνάω); a favourite figure of Cicero’s for governing (Lewis & Short).

  • praesideō, praesidēre, praesēdī — govern, preside over (a province)

    verb, second conjugation, with the dative (later also the accusative) · also used · classical · Traupman 323

Examples

  • īra furor brevis est; animum rege, quī nisi pāret, imperat

    anger is a short madness; rule your temper, for if it does not obey, it commandsHor. Ep. 1.2.62–63

  • Rēgnat, nōn regitur, quī nīl nisi quod vult facit.

    whoever does nothing but what he wants is the ruler, not the ruledPublil. Sent. R 19

  • quattuor rōbustōs fīliōs, quīnque fīliās, tantam domum, tantās clientēlās Appius regēbat et caecus et senex

    four strong sons, five daughters, so great a household, so many clients: Appius ruled them all, blind and old as he wasCic. Sen. 37

  • rem pūblicam gubernāre

    to govern the countryTraupman 179

See also government, rule, in charge.
